thread:
Maya R: Folks — need a compact one-pager (single sheet) AEs can hand to enterprise prospects. Must cover security, SLA highlights, and deployment choices (hosted / dedicated / private). Draft in GDoc: https://docs.google.com/example-deploy-sell-sheet
Sam: Can we squeeze a 1-2 line latency vs cost note? Keep it very short.
Jordan P: Also add a tiny tech pre-req list customers always ask for. I can paste examples.
Tess (Content): I put a hero + three bullets in the doc. Copy below for quick feedback:
Tess (Content): ```
Hero: Run LLMs in production — predictably, privately, and economically.
Bullets:
• Enterprise controls: KMS/HSM, SOC2-grade audit logs, RBAC
• Deployment choices: Hosted API, Reserved Dedicated, Private VPC / on-prem
• Predictable economics: SLA-backed throughput, batching & quantization advice
```
Kai (Sales): Love it. Add a 3-line "AE talk track" and a 1-line competitor differentiator in the footer.
Elliot (Tech PM): For SLAs, call out our p99 availability target and a one-sentence fallback: route to compatible hosted variant if dedicated is saturated. Also a tiny ascii flow for the visual: Client -> Routing -> [Dedicated (preferred)] -> Hosted fallback.
Sam: Draft for latency vs cost (one-liner): "Choose dedicated low-latency pools for p99-sensitive routes; use hosted + quantization for cost-optimized batch/async workloads."
Jordan P: Pre-req checklist (copy from doc):
• VPC peering or customer proxy / IP allowlist (private vs hosted cases)
• KMS/HSM integration and key rotation policy
• Audit log retention and export endpoints
• Network egress rules (443 outbound to registry / telemetry endpoints)
• Expected token volumes and maximum context length
Tess (Content): I tightened the hero and shortened bullets to fit one page. AE talk track (3 lines):
"We give you a consistent API across hosted, reserved, and private so your app stays stable.
We optimize routing, batching, and quantization to lower cost without surprising regressions.
SLA-backed capacity and clear fallbacks keep production apps reliable."
Kai (Sales): Perfect. Footer differentiator suggestion: "Deploy anywhere, operate everywhere — unified runtime and visibility."
Maya R: Nice. Can someone confirm phrasing on the SLA bullet? Keep it short: mention p99 availability, throughput guarantees on Dedicated, and automatic fallback to hosted variant.
Elliot (Tech PM): Short SLA line suggestion: "p99 availability target; Dedicated offers throughput SLAs and automated hosted fallback when capacity is constrained."
Sam: Small layout suggestion: move "Enterprise controls" to the top of the bullets (sales prefers that ordering).
Tess (Content): Swapped ordering. I also mocked a tiny callout box with the latency vs cost blurb and the ascii routing.
Tess (Content): Callout text: "Latency vs cost — Dedicated pools for low-latency p99 paths; hosted + quantization for cost-efficient batch/async."
Tess (Content): Visual: "Client -> Routing -> [Dedicated pool (preferred)] -> Hosted fallback (compatible model)"
Jordan P: I pasted the tech pre-reqs into the doc and added short notes for each (e.g., recommended retention for audit logs).
Maya R: Great. Plan: Tess finalize PDF mock by Thu 4pm, internal review Thu EOD, ship Fri AM. Sam / Jordan / Kai — finalize your bits by Thu noon.
deploy-bot: Preview built: https://redwood-internal.preview/sell-sheet/1912345678 (PDF + PNG) :white_check_mark:
Kai (Sales): Approved (minor nit: swap bullets so controls first — done).
Jordan P: Approved.
Sam: Approved.
Tess (Content): Final PDF exported and uploaded to the doc. Ready for final walkthrough.
Maya R: Thank you. We'll use this as the AE quick-hit for inbound demo requests and link to it from the webinar slide deck. Please drop single-line approvals or tiny edits by Thu 5pm.
Kai (Sales): Approved — looks sharp.
Maya R: Closing thread — final assets live in the marketing drive and linked in the preview above.
